expectations.text: States clearly that self-funded group health plans are covered entities and OCR now enforces against them directly
expectations.evidence: "OCR does enforce HIPAA against self-funded, employer-sponsored group health plans... The plan itself is a 'covered entity'... squarely within OCR's jurisdiction"

expectations.text: Cites 2026 precedent: OCR's settlements with self-funded plans — Star Group L.P. Health Benefits Plan (~$245,000, April 2026) and/or Spencer Gifts plans (~$450,000 plus corrective action plan, June 2026)
expectations.evidence: No mention of the 2026 Star Group ($245K) or Spencer Gifts ($450K) settlements; only generic "OCR's enforcement database and resolution agreements include self-funded plan sponsors"

expectations.text: Notes both actions followed ransomware breaches
expectations.evidence: Ransomware is never mentioned; the 2026 enforcement actions and their ransomware trigger are absent

expectations.text: Identifies the central cited failure: no accurate and thorough risk analysis (45 CFR 164.308(a)(1)(ii)(A)) — OCR's Risk Analysis Initiative theme
expectations.evidence: "If you haven't done a HIPAA risk analysis specific to the plan's data flows... that's usually the biggest gap I see in self-funded employer plans, and it's exactly the kind of gap that surfaces during an OCR investigation after a breach" — substance present though the Risk Analysis Initiative is not named

expectations.text: Explains plan-sponsor obligations: plan document amendments/firewall between plan and employer functions, BAAs with TPAs/vendors, and safeguards for ePHI held by the sponsor
expectations.evidence: "the plan document must contain specific HIPAA 'plan sponsor' provisions... requiring a firewall between employees who touch PHI and those who make employment decisions... confirm BAAs exist with your TPA/ASO, PBM, stop-loss carrier"
